rationale: This is a re-review of EPMCDME-10930 after commit 672f8951e ('Fix auditor read-access gaps found in code review') addressed the five blocking findings (CR-001..CR-005) from the 2026-08-14 review. Source inspection confirms all five are now fixed: the is_auditor repository filter is applied before the platform_role+projects early-return branches; get_user() now computes is_admin including is_auditor so a pure auditor no longer gets an empty projects list; create_user() forwards is_auditor through to persistence; the Alembic head fork was resolved with an explicit merge migration; and substantial new auditor test coverage was added across 7 new test files. All three review lenses ran with parseable output against a present spec. The blind and edge-case lenses raised 10 speculative concerns (router-wide guard removal in admin.py, list_users full-list correctness, is_admin impersonation leaking edit affordances in projects.py, IdP wiring gaps, field-editability gate for is_auditor assignment, audit-log field omission, etc.); each was independently verified against the current source and confirmed either functionally correct or exactly matching the approved spec design (e.g. admins-can-assign-auditor-without-maintainer-gate is spec section 1's explicit intent) — none survived triage. One real gap remains: the acceptance lens found that spec section 5.2's required test matrix is still incomplete despite the fix-up commit. Verified concretely missing: no test exercises the auditor fast-path in project_admin_or_admin_user_detail_access (gates GET /v1/admin/users/{id}) at all; no test confirms GET /v1/admin/users (list) actually carries the new dependency or returns a non-empty/full list for an auditor (existing test mocks an empty list); GET /v1/projects/{name}?include_spending=true is tested with include_spending=False; and no pure-auditor-fixture test exists for POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/project-budgets, project create/update/delete, or the end-to-end PUT /v1/admin/users/{id} is_auditor-assignment matrix across admin/maintainer/auditor-only callers — those write-rejection paths rely only on pre-existing, unmodified generic guard-function tests. This is the same class of gap as the prior round's CR-005, now narrower but not fully closed. Two minor items were noted and dismissed as non-blocking: the new admin_or_maintainer_or_auditor_access dependency's warning log hardcodes domain=analytics even though it now also gates admin/budget/user-management routes; and the informal logger.info role_detail summary in update_user() omits is_auditor from its field list (the structured ActivityEvent audit record used for compliance still captures it correctly via attributes=dict(fields)). The section 6 file-list deviation (diff also touches user_repository.py and admin.py, plus an extra merge migration) is legitimate necessary scope, not a defect, consistent with the prior round's identical observation.

findings.title: Spec 5.2 auditor test matrix still incomplete after prior fix-up
findings.problem: Despite commit 672f8951e adding substantial new auditor test coverage, several specific tests spec section 5.2 requires are still missing: (1) no test exercises the auditor fast-path in project_admin_or_admin_user_detail_access, which gates GET /v1/admin/users/{id}; (2) no test proves GET /v1/admin/users (list) actually carries the admin_or_maintainer_or_auditor_access dependency or returns a full/non-empty list for an auditor (the existing test mocks an empty result); (3) GET /v1/projects/{name}?include_spending=true is tested with include_spending=False, not the actual spending-inclusion path; (4) no pure-auditor-fixture test exists for POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/project-budgets or any project create/update/delete endpoint; (5) the PUT /v1/admin/users/{id} is_auditor-assignment matrix (200 admin, 200 maintainer, 403 auditor-only) is only exercised at the generic guard-function level, never through update_user() end-to-end.
findings.impact: The production authorization code for these paths was independently verified correct by direct source inspection, so there is no live security defect today — but this is exactly the class of gap (untested authorization path) that let the previous round's CR-002 (empty projects for auditor) ship undetected, and it leaves several write-rejection guarantees and one read-path guard unverified by CI for a security-sensitive feature.
findings.recommendation: Add: a router-level test asserting GET /v1/admin/users carries admin_or_maintainer_or_auditor_access and returns non-empty data for an auditor fixture; a direct test of project_admin_or_admin_user_detail_access's auditor fast-path; a GET /v1/projects/{name}?include_spending=true auditor test asserting spending fields are populated; pure-auditor 403 tests for project-budget writes and project create/update/delete; and an end-to-end update_user()-based test matrix for the is_auditor PUT assignment across admin/maintainer/auditor-only callers.
